s1.context: A conversation between a university student and a sports centre receptionist about gym membership.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Good morning, Willowbrook Sports Centre. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Hello. I'm a university student and I'd like to find out about joining the gym.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Of course. Let me take some details. Can I have your surname, please?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: It's Harper. That's H, A, R, P, E, R.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Thank you, Mr Harper. Now, as a student you can choose our student membership, which is cheaper than the standard one.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: That sounds good. How much is it?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The student membership is twenty-two pounds a month. The standard membership is thirty-five pounds.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Twenty-two pounds is fine. Is there any special offer if I sign up for a full year?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Yes. If you sign a twelve-month contract, you get a free personal training session in your first week.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Excellent. And when is the gym usually busiest? I'd rather avoid the crowds.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: It's very quiet in the mornings and at lunchtime, but it gets crowded in the evening, after five o'clock.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Then I'll try to come in the mornings. What time do the different facilities open?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The pool opens at six in the morning, the gym opens at seven, and the sauna doesn't open until nine.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Great. Do I need to do anything before I start?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Yes, all new members must attend a short induction. It runs every Saturday morning at ten o'clock.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Perfect. I'll come along this Saturday.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Wonderful. We look forward to seeing you, Mr Harper.

s2.context: A guide gives new students a walking tour of the Northfield University campus. Look at the map while you listen.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Welcome to Northfield University, and congratulations on starting your studies. I'm going to give you a short tour of the main campus. Please look at the map in front of you. We are standing at the main entrance, at the bottom of the map.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Walk straight up the central path. On your left, near the entrance, you'll see the student café. That's the building marked C. On your right, at the same level, is the health centre, marked F.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Continue as far as the fountain in the middle of the path. Directly on your left, opposite the fountain, is the library, marked B. The library is the building you'll use most, so remember that you need to swipe your student card to get in.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Opposite the library, on the right of the fountain, is the science block, marked E.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: At the far end of the path, on the top left, is the main lecture theatre, marked A. And in the top right corner is the sports hall, marked D.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: A few useful points before we finish. During exam weeks, the library and the computer lab stay open around the clock, but the café and the sports hall close at ten in the evening.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The tour ends at the sports hall, where each of you will collect a welcome pack. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your first week.
